planting.note: Pot in spring into a high-organic, well-drained aroid mix in bright indirect light; comb-leaf philodendron grows in a bird's-nest-like rosette habit rather than climbing like many philodendron species.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light in a chunky, organic-rich, well-drained potting mix; comb-leaf philodendron is native to Venezuela and northern Brazil, forming a bird's-nest-habit rosette of deeply pinnately cut leaves rather than climbing like many of its relatives. Keep the soil evenly moist but never soggy, allowing the surface to dry slightly between waterings. It has no frost tolerance and is grown as a houseplant or greenhouse specimen in temperate climates, outdoor-hardy only in true tropical zones 9b-11.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a chunky, bark-based aroid mix in bright indirect light; Melinonii grows as a self-heading, semi-climbing rosette rather than a true vine.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light in a chunky, bark-based aroid potting mix with good drainage; Melinonii Philodendron is an unusual self-heading or semi-climbing rosette form from lowland South America, distinct from the more familiar vining philodendron growth habit. Water once the substrate is roughly 30-50% dry, and provide warm temperatures (65-84°F) with 50-60% humidity for best growth. It has no frost tolerance and is grown strictly as a houseplant outside the deep tropics.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a chunky, airy aroid mix with a moss pole for support in bright indirect light; Fibrosum needs high humidity and a climbing support, as a hemiepiphyte.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light on a moss pole or similar support, in a chunky, well-drained aroid mix; Fibrosum Philodendron is an Ecuadorian climbing hemiepiphyte prized for velvety, bullate (quilted-textured) leaves and fuzzy reddish petioles. It needs high humidity, 70-90%, to maintain its best leaf texture, and should be watered once the mix is about 30-50% dry. It has no frost tolerance and is grown strictly as a houseplant or greenhouse specimen outside the tropics.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a well-drained aroid mix with a moss pole or trellis for support in bright indirect light; this vigorous climbing vine needs ample room to grow upward.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light on a moss pole or trellis, in a well-drained potting mix; Three-Lobed Philodendron is a vigorous climbing vine native to Central and South America, bearing distinctive deeply tri-lobed leaves. Water once the top inch of soil has dried and maintain humidity above 60% and warm temperatures of 65-80°F for best growth. It has no frost tolerance and is grown strictly as a houseplant or greenhouse vine outside the deep tropics.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a well-drained aroid mix with a trellis or pole for support in bright indirect light; Jacquinii's leaf shape elongates noticeably as the plant matures.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light on a trellis or pole, in a well-drained potting mix; Jacquinii Philodendron is a climbing aroid native from Mexico through northern South America and the western Caribbean, bearing glossy, heart-shaped juvenile leaves that elongate noticeably as the plant matures. Let the top few centimeters of soil dry before watering again, and maintain humidity above 50%. It is less commonly stocked in US specialty trade than some other candidates here, so sourcing may take a bit more searching; it has no frost tolerance and is grown as a houseplant outside the tropics.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a well-drained epiphyte mix in bright indirect to moderate light; Linnaei tolerates lower light better than most philodendron species, making it an unusually forgiving choice.

directions: Grow in moderate to bright indirect light in a well-drained, chunky epiphyte mix; Linnaei Philodendron is a semi-succulent true epiphyte or hemiepiphyte from Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, bearing obovate (egg-shaped) leaves. It is noted as unusually easy-care for the genus, tolerating lower light levels better than most philodendron species and needing only moderate humidity of 40-60%. Water once the top inch of substrate is dry; it has no frost tolerance and is grown strictly as a houseplant outside the tropics.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a well-drained aroid mix in moderate indirect light; Bonplandii tolerates average household humidity better than many collector anthuriums.

directions: Grow in moderate indirect light in a well-drained potting mix; Bonplandii Anthurium is a resilient strap-leaved, bird's-nest-type South American species that tolerates ordinary household humidity better than many of the more demanding collector anthuriums. Let the soil dry slightly between waterings rather than keeping it constantly saturated. It has no frost tolerance and is grown as a houseplant in temperate climates, making it a reasonably beginner-friendly entry into the genus.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a chunky epiphyte mix in bright indirect light; Balaoanum is considered one of the easier 'rare' anthuriums, tolerating humidity as low as 50% and temperatures down to about 60°F.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light in a chunky, airy epiphyte mix; Balaoanum Anthurium is an Ecuadorian epiphytic species regarded as one of the more forgiving 'rare' anthuriums in cultivation, tolerating humidity as low as 50% and temperatures down to roughly 60°F, more than most collector anthuriums can handle. Water once the top 2-3 centimeters of substrate dries. It has no frost tolerance and is grown as a houseplant or greenhouse specimen outside the deep tropics.

planting.note: Pot in spring into evenly moist, well-drained soil in bright indirect light; Obtusum grows terrestrially rather than as an epiphyte, distinguishing it from the already-present Anthurium scandens.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light in evenly moist, well-drained soil; Obtusum Anthurium is a terrestrial, bird's-nest-type species distributed from Belize to Bolivia, distinguished from the already-grown epiphytic Anthurium scandens by its ground-rooted habit and an erect rather than reflexed white spathe. It needs consistently high humidity and steady moisture without waterlogging. It has no frost tolerance and is grown as a houseplant in temperate climates.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a well-drained epiphyte mix in moderate indirect light; Formosum needs high humidity, 70-80%, to maintain its deeply veined upright leaves.

directions: Grow in moderate indirect light in a well-drained, airy potting mix; Formosum Anthurium is an epiphytic South American species with elongated, deeply veined, upright leaves. It needs consistently high humidity, 70-80%, and regular watering balanced with good drainage to avoid root rot. It has no frost tolerance and is grown strictly as a houseplant outside the deep tropics.

planting.note: Pot in spring into a well-drained aroid mix with a support for climbing, in bright indirect to dappled light; Kunthii's distinctive finger-like palmate leaves set it apart from most other anthurium species.

directions: Grow in bright indirect to dappled light on a climbing support, in a well-drained potting mix; Kunthii Anthurium is a climbing subshrub or epiphyte ranging from Central America to Bolivia, distinguished by distinctive finger-like, palmate leaves in the Dactylophyllium section of the genus, unlike the simple leaves of most anthuriums. Water once the top 3 centimeters of substrate dries, and maintain humidity between 60-80%. It has no frost tolerance and is grown strictly as a houseplant outside the tropics.
